title: Big factorials and digit sums
description:
Write two functions with BigInt:

- `factorial(n)` returns `n!` as a BigInt for a whole number `n` from 0 up (`factorial(0)` is `1n`). A negative or fractional `n` throws `RangeError`.
- `digitSum(big)` returns the sum of the decimal digits of a non-negative BigInt, as an ordinary number.

```javascript
factorial(25);            // 15511210043330985984000000n
digitSum(factorial(100)); // 648
```
hints: Start from `1n` and loop with a BigInt counter: `for (let i = 2n; i <= BigInt(n); i++)`. Mixing `1` and `1n` in one calculation throws.
The digits of a BigInt are the characters of `big.toString()`.
